A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 17-page XRIR paper, including supplementary Sections 7–13. Complete text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the research content is identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated and real-room evaluations, single-room prediction experiments, and component, fine-tuning, and dataset-scale analyses in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results in Tables 1–7 and the associated qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The XRIR architecture, geometric and reference-RIR encoders, fusion and weighting procedure, losses, inference, and supplementary single-room adaptation are identical.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ACOUSTICROOMS, four real Hearing-Anything-Anywhere environments, and six SoundSpaces 1.0 Replica scenes, with identical task and scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical comparator membership, including the random, interpolation, nearest-neighbor, Few-Shot RIR, Diff-RIR, NAF, and INRAS baselines in their respective experiments.

E3.justification: The splits, reference counts, preprocessing, model configurations, fine-tuning procedures, and evaluation metrics in the main text and supplementary experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, pretraining/fine-tuning comparison, dataset-scale study, and qualitative waveform and acoustic-map analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version provides repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported performance.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–7 and the qualitative figures are unchanged. For example, XRIR with K=8 retains unseen-split errors of 0.055 s EDT, 1.457 dB C50, and 10.53% T60.

T1.justification: The task definitions, coordinate transformations, attention and weighting equations, loss definitions, and supplementary single-room formulation are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about cross-room generalization, the ACOUSTICROOMS dataset, predictive performance, and sim-to-real transfer.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including explanations of Few-Shot RIR performance, noise-related T60 limitations, and degraded depth inputs in Apartment 2.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, simulation settings, preprocessing, fine-tuning instructions, and research-resource access information are identical, including supplementary Sections 9–11.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical, including comparisons with prior cross-room prediction methods and acoustic simulation datasets.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 14 Apr 2025, to v2, dated 4 Jun 2025. All paper prose, headings, terminology, and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. All nine figures, seven tables, captions, and body layout are unchanged; pages 2–17 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information are identical throughout both PDFs and their appendices. The version-stamp and metadata updates do not meaningfully affect overall paper quality.
